transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-16
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~72 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood SE), Samir (Redwood CSM), Lena (Redwood Solutions), Alex (Novalux ML), Priya (Novalux Product), Leo (Novalux Infra), Hannah (Novalux Security)
Links shared: Redwood dedicated pricing (drive link), pilot benchmark sheet (drive link), security pack (redwood.com/security-docs)

Summary: quick Q4 check-in focused on adoption cadence, current cost burn, reliability incidents over last 30 days, and security next steps for private deployment. Agreed to run a pilot benchmark and exchange traffic patterns and security artifacts.

00:00 Jordan (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. Quick roll call?
00:08 Alex (Head of ML): Alex here.
00:09 Priya (VP Product): Priya here.
00:11 Leo (Infra): Leo on the line.
00:12 Hannah (Security): Hannah here.
00:13 Jordan: Great. Maya and I are from Redwood, Samir and Lena as well. We'll try to keep this to about an hour, 70-ish minutes.

02:05 Jordan: High level — want to cover adoption, some of the cost patterns you've been seeing, reliability incidents, and then the security checklist we talked about last time and next steps for the pilot. Priya, can you kick off with what success looks for Q4?
02:18 Priya: Sure, thanks. For Q4 our top two bets are increasing chat-based product adoption on checkout flows and lowering inference cost per transaction by 25%. We also need zero customer-visible outages — like anything that affects response times over 2 seconds is a blocker for the product team.
02:40 Jordan: Got it, that maps to what we saw. Alex, how's the model rollout going? Any surprises?
02:46 Alex: Overall good, but we did see a couple of latency spikes coinciding with the 11am east coast traffic surge. Some requests fell back to smaller model variants because cache warming was slow. I think there’s an opportunity to tune prefix caching and KV cache retention — sorry if I butchered the terms — but basically the warmup pattern isn't hitting our steady-state.
03:20 Maya (SE): That makes sense; KV cache plus proactive warming can help. Also, if you pin a dedicated pool for the primary endpoint during peak windows, you avoid the cold-start rerouting. There’s a tradeoff between reserved capacity costs and the risk of model fallback.
03:45 Leo: Can you quantify that tradeoff? Right now our cost per request went up 18% during peaks because of retries and fallbacks.
03:53 Maya: Roughly, a small dedicated pool sized to your 95th percentile peak would add about 12–15% to committed monthly burn but reduce tail latency by up to 40–60% depending on workload. We can run a simulation with your traffic to refine that.
04:20 Priya: We can consider a hybrid — hosted for off-peak and dedicated for peak windows, but SSO and data residency requirements push us toward private. Hannah, does that sound right?
04:33 Hannah: Yes, we prefer private control plane for PII flows. Also need KMS integration and audit logs forwarded to our Splunk. SOC2 Type II is a must; we want to see recent attestations.
04:44 Jordan: We shared the security pack link in chat. It includes SOC2 docs, SAML SSO guide, and KMS/HSM integration notes. We'll re-send and highlight the attestation dates.
04:58 Samir (CSM): Quick note: we've seen customers use Private Redwood with VPC peering and a private control plane, then keep metrics shipped to customer logging via our secure forwarder. That pattern might fit Novalux.

06:10 Alex: On reliability, we had an incident on 11/02 where a model rollout triggered a version mismatch in the routing layer; about 3 minutes of increased 5xx. Our oncall latched onto it but we want Redwood's rollback policies tightened.
06:32 Maya: Sorry about that, we investigated and adjusted the canary thresholds — the auto-fallback should have triggered earlier. We're proposing tightening the canary success criteria and adding a preflight lightweight health check during rollouts.
06:52 Leo: Will that add latency to deploys? Our release window is small.
06:57 Maya: Minimal, the preflight is a tiny litmus test hitting model health endpoints; it adds a few seconds but avoids full rollbacks. We'll include a deploy step in the pilot runbook.

09:15 Priya: Let's talk numbers — what are we forecasting for November burn with the proposed dedicated buffer?
09:22 Jordan: Based on the initial telemetry we've seen, adding a small dedicated pool for peak windows bumps committed spend by ~14% but reduces expected overage and tail cost by about 20% across the month. I'll share a modeled spreadsheet.
09:38 Priya: We'd like to see a scenario that keeps monthly cost within a 10% variance of current budget while guaranteeing 99.9% p95 latency.
09:46 Jordan: We'll run three scenarios: conservative reserved (95th percentile), hybrid scheduled reserved (peak windows only), and on-demand with burst (higher variable).

12:05 Hannah: Regarding security: can Redwood support customer-managed KMS where keys never leave our HSM? Also need forwardable audit logs and retention for 1 year at a minimum.
12:21 Lena (Solutions): Yes, our Private package supports KMS/HSM integration and we can configure log forwarding to your Splunk instance. Retention controls are customer-configurable. We'll confirm exact retention and export formats.
12:34 Hannah: Also need SSO via SAML and fine-grained RBAC so product managers can't see raw request payloads.
12:42 Maya: RBAC is supported; we can mask PII at the token level and provide token-level auditability. We'll include the RBAC matrix in the security doc.

15:00 Alex: Pilot scope — we want a 2-week pilot that simulates peak traffic, includes a canary rollout, and verifies multi-region failover. Also need to validate token-level cost attribution for product experiments.
15:18 Maya: For the pilot we'll need your traffic histograms and a 48-hour sample log. We recommended a 2–4 hour benchmark window during your 11am east-coast peak; we can run repeated bursts to test cache warm-up.
15:35 Leo: We can provide those. Also want to run the pilot in a staging VPC that mirrors production network egress rates.
15:41 Samir: Noted. We'll put together the runbook and the test checklist.

18:10 Priya: One ask — support for model quantization recommendations. Our models vary and we want guidance on when int8 vs fp16 makes sense to hit cost targets without regressions.
18:25 Maya: Our Optimize toolkit gives quantization suggestions per-model and per-workload, with expected latency/cost deltas and a rollback path. We'll attach example quantization profiles from a similar retail workload.
18:40 Alex: Be careful — some of our rerank tasks degrade with lossy quantization. We'll want to gate that with eval prompt sets.
18:50 Lena: We can hook our eval regression alerts to your evals; Redwood's quality monitoring will flag regressions tied to prompt sets.

22:05 Jordan: Quick product update — new console view for per-route token breakdowns drops next month; should help you slice cost to product feature.
22:16 Priya: Helpful. Can that export to CSV or connect to our internal billing pipeline?
22:21 Jordan: Yes both; we'll show export steps in the demo.

25:30 Hannah: For compliance, what's the process for annual penetration testing of Private installs?
25:38 Lena: We run quarterly internal assessments and can coordinate a joint penetration test or allow you to run your third-party pentest with our guidance and a temporary scoped window. We'll send the pentest runbook.
25:50 Hannah: Great.

28:45 Alex: A few operational asks — can we get token-level cost attribution by service (chat vs embeddings vs rerank)? Our finance team wants product-level chargeback.
28:58 Samir: That's available in the Console; we can map token usage to product routes and create a per-route dashboard. We'll prepare a sample dashboard for Novalux.
29:10 Priya: Also, can Redwood commit to a 30-minute rollback SLA for P1s?
29:17 Jordan: Our SLAs vary by plan; for Dedicated we have tighter operational SLOs and an enterprise escalation path. We'll include the SLA matrix in the follow-up.

34:00 Leo: Networking question — does Private support VPC peering and also proxy egress through our NAT? Our infra constraints require fixed egress IPs.
34:12 Lena: Yes, Private supports VPC peering and static egress options; we'll document NAT/static IPs.

38:55 Priya: Any blockers from Redwood side to start the pilot?
38:59 Maya: We just need your traffic sample and security points of contact. Also need agreement on the pilot window and success criteria — e.g., p95 latency below 1.2s and no functional regression on evals.
39:18 Alex: That sounds fair. We'll define success criteria and share it.

42:00 Jordan: Recap — Redwood will: 1) send detailed dedicated vs hosted TCO scenarios, 2) push the security pack with attestation dates and RBAC matrix, 3) prepare pilot runbook and dashboard samples. Novalux will: share traffic samples, security questionnaire answers, and decide on pilot dates.

43:10 Priya: Can we get a timeline for those deliverables?
43:14 Jordan: Yes — TCO and pricing by 11/19, security artifacts by 11/20, pilot runbook by 11/24. Pilot to start week of 11/30 pending materials.

55:05 Hannah: One final note — we may need data residency in EU for some markets; what's Redwood's posture?
55:12 Lena: Redwood supports region pinning for deployments; for EU residency we can provision model serving in EU regions with private networking. We'll follow up with region-specific compliance notes.
55:30 Hannah: Thanks.

70:30 Jordan: Thanks everyone, appreciate the time. We'll follow up with the artifacts and get the pilot scheduled.

Meeting end.

Notes: Natural transcription noise present — some words transcribed imperfectly (e.g., "KV cache" sometimes appears as "K V cache"), occasional speaker attribution hiccups.
